title: Benchmark signal sleuth session — microburst & tail-latency triage
body:
Meeting notes:

Summary:
- Ran a 'sleuth' session to hunt a recurring tail-latency bump seen across nightly regression runs. Goal: reproduce and isolate signal to kernel, batching, or KV-cache temperature.
- High-level symptom: 99.9th latency spikes (~50-80ms above baseline) on mixed-sequence workload during 2-6 QPS bursts. Throughput steady; p50/p95 fine.

What we ran:
- Harness: sleuthbench v0.3 (new harness that injects bursty inter-arrival patterns and records per-token compute time).
- Configs:
  * model: resnet-style-lm-13b-8k (quantized int8-fast)
  * batcher: continuous-batcher v2 (max batch 16, timeout 12ms)
  * kernel variant: cuda-opt-v4 vs cuda-opt-v5
  * KV policy: no-prefetch, prefix-cache size 8k
- Command snippets:
  * ./sleuthbench --qps-profile burst-2to6.json --seq-mix mixed-1-512 --runs 120 --collect-traces
  * k-run: ./run_kernel_compare.sh --kernels cuda-opt-v4,cuda-opt-v5 --samples 50

Observations:
- Spike pattern correlates with sudden queue-depth oscillations when inter-arrival jumps > 100ms.
- cuda-opt-v5 reduced average latency by ~8ms but increased tail amplitude (higher 99.9) in 3/5 runs.
- When we forced batcher timeout to 6ms, tail spikes decreased but p50 increased slightly; trade-off noted.
- KV-cache temperature: cold-start windows (after 30s idle) show higher token compute time; but spikes persisted even when cache hot → not pure KV issue.
- Hardware: seen on A100-80GB and on V100 in staging; suggests not hardware-specific.
- Trace capture shows a cluster of tasks waiting on 'serialize_io' stage before model_compute in spike runs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batcher edge case under bursty arrivals: short-lived over-aggregation causes serialization backlog ('serialize_io' pressure) causing microtail.
2) Kernel scheduling preemption: cuda-opt-v5 schedules kernels that conflict with background IO tasks under certain stream ordering.
3) Host-side GC/alloc stall when large batch sizes hit ephemeral allocator thresholds.

Quick checks done:
- Forced single-stream execution: tail reduced but throughput down 12% -> implicates stream contention.
- Re-run with preallocated allocator: small reduction in spike occurrences (~15%).
- Re-run with jitter-smoothed arrival (add uniform 0-10ms): spikes largely disappear.

Immediate next experiments (owners/due):
- Jun: Add micro-profiling around serialize_io and run with per-call async IO counters (due 2026-09-27).
- Marta: Instrument batcher to emit batch-formation histograms and annotate traces with batch_id (due 2026-09-25).
- Liam: Run kernel-schedule trace on cuda-opt-v5 with stream-affinity toggled; capture cublas/cudnn timelines (due 2026-09-28).
- Aisha: Run long-duration sleuthbench with steady-state JIT warm start to measure spike rate per million requests (due 2026-09-30).

Actionable mitigations we can try in short-term:
- Lower batcher max timeout to 6ms for bursty tiers in Dedicated pools (will reduce tail but accept slight p50 cost).
- Introduce arrival jittering gate in router for hosted API for small bursts (adds 1–3ms latency but reduces tail spikes for interactive apps).
- Preallocate large ephemeral arena on hosts to avoid allocator stalls under rare large-batch events.

Open questions:
- Why does cuda-opt-v5 raise 99.9 but lower p50 — is there a scheduling trade-off we can tune in kernel selection? (Liam follow-up)
- Is 'serialize_io' a generic name covering multiple things (output postprocessing, tokenizer, metrics?) — need finer labels in traces. (Jun)
- Can we reproduce in private on-prem package where networking and IO stack differ? (Aisha)

Notes for routing/ops:
- If we flip batcher timeout in prod for burst-protected routes, apply canary to 5% of traffic and monitor p50/p99.9 and cost delta.
- Suggested dashboard widgets: batch-formation-rate, serialize_io-latency, arrival-IA distribution, kernel-variant breakdown.

Attachments / Links:
- sleuthbench run artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/sleuth/2026-09-23/run-17/{traces,profiles}. (internal)
- Quick flame graphs: https://flame.example.com/run-17 (private)

Decisions made:
- Short-term: try batcher timeout reduction on dedicated canary and add arrival jittering in router for noisy routes.
- Mid-term: improve batcher instrumentation and add a kernel-scheduling trace flag to cublas/cudnn wrapper.

Meeting attendees:
- Aisha Romero (scribe), Jun Park, Marta Singh, Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai (observability), Omar Reyes (platform)

Follow-up meeting: 2026-09-29 10:00 PT (30m) — agenda: review instrumented traces and canary metrics.

Raw logs/snippets:
- Sample trace id: trace-20260923-run17-abc123
- kprobe output excerpt: node=worker-03 serialize_io tail90=32ms wait_count=4

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep sleuthbench config in repo under /experiments/sleuthbench and add a doc on best-effort repro steps.
- Consider small RFC to expose batcher timeout as route-level override in Console for rapid mitigation.
